question: Can a class-balanced, CV-tuned LightGBM that uses the few confirmed fraud labels beat a label-free unsupervised anomaly detector on time-ordered credit-card fraud detection?
method: Time-sorted 70/30 split; Isolation Forest (label-free) vs class-balanced LightGBM with 3-fold stratified CV random search on the training period; PR-AUC on the later test period; seeds 42-44.
baseline: Isolation Forest (sklearn, 200 trees), label-free, fitted on training features only.
improved: LightGBM with class_weight='balanced', hyperparameters chosen by 3-fold stratified CV random search (8 candidates) on training data using training fraud labels.
notes: Best CV params: {'reg_lambda': 1.0, 'num_leaves': 15, 'n_estimators': 200, 'min_child_samples': 20, 'learning_rate': 0.1}. Single time-ordered split; test fraud count is small so estimates are noisy. CV is stratified, not time-aware. The Isolation Forest is a generic label-free stand-in, not the paper's GraphGuard method and not a re-implementation of it. Secondary F1 and recall use a top-1% alert rate. std is population std over 3 seeds. Full dataset used (no subsampling) since runtime is well within budget. The features are PCA components, so no graph structure is used.
